{
  "need": "Status",
  "secondary": { "name": "Belonging" },
  "read": "After a big win, players are riding a status high — individual stats and highlight plays felt like the path to mattering, and the scoreboard validated that instinct. The belonging piece shows up underneath: if the culture rewards individual shine, fitting in means playing that way. No one feels urgency to change what just worked.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Lecture them about being selfish right after a win — it feels righteous, but it kills the energy and makes you the enemy of their joy, so they tune you out or resent you instead of hearing the message." },
  "mentorMove": "Acknowledge the win fully and without asterisks first, then redirect status toward the team: frame playing together as the higher-level skill that separates good teams from great ones, and treat them as capable of that next level right now.",
  "holdFirm": ["The standard is team-first ball — that does not move because the score was lopsided.", "Every player will be held to making the right play, not the flashy one."],
  "stayFlexible": ["Let them celebrate the win genuinely before you shift the conversation.", "Invite players to name what team-first ball looks like in their own words rather than dictating it."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Okay, bring it in. That was a big win — you competed hard and you earned that result. I am not taking that away from you, not for a second." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "I want to ask you something and I want a real answer. When you watch great teams — the ones that people actually talk about years later — what do you notice about the way they move the ball? What makes them different?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Right. So here is what I saw tonight: a lot of individual moments, and the score let us get away with it. I need us to figure out together what it looks like when this group plays at that next level — because the scoreboard tonight is not the ceiling, it is just the floor. What would have to change?" },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding us to team-first ball every possession from here forward — not because I am unhappy with the win, but because I have high standards for what this group can become and I know you can play at that level. That is the standard. How we build it together, I want your voice in that." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Keep referencing team-first moments in practice with specific praise — call out the assist, the screen, the right pass over the easy look — so status gets attached to those behaviors and the culture slowly redefines what it means to shine on this team."
}
situation: My team won big and played selfish, ugly ball the entire game.
